hook.text: Several times in Earth's history, oceans lost nearly all their oxygen—killing most marine life.

buildup.text: These 'ocean anoxic events' occurred during periods of extreme warming—when circulation slowed and oxygen dropped.

discovery.text: Black shale layers in the rock record mark these events—organic matter preserved because nothing could decompose it.

twist.text: The worst—during the Permian extinction—killed 96% of marine species. Warming drove the suffocation.

climax.text: Today's deoxygenation mirrors early stages of past events—we're far from those extremes, but the direction matches.

punchline.text: History shows what happens when oceans lose oxygen—it's catastrophic.

quiz.question: What are ocean anoxic events?
options: Periods when oceans lost most of their oxygen, killing marine life
